title: MCP server
intro: Lets assistants such as Claude Code or Codex read the structure of your databases and, on the connections you enable, run read-only queries or, with your approval of each one, make changes. It works only on this machine and while DBine is open.
warning: Query results are sent to the assistant's model. Enable reading only on connections where that is fine.
serverHelp: Listens on 127.0.0.1 only: it doesn't accept connections from other machines or from browser pages.
portHelp: If another program is using it, pick a different one and update your clients' configuration.
defaultLevelHelp: What clients can do with connections that don't have their own level.

levelHelp.schema: Databases, objects and their structure; no data.
levelHelp.read: Also sample rows, read-only queries and execution plans.
levelHelp.write: Also changes to data and structure: DBine shows you each one and nothing runs until you approve it.

clientsHelp: Each client has its own token. DBine stores only its fingerprint (SHA-256): the token is shown just once.
revokeConfirm: Revoke “{{name}}”? It can no longer connect, effective immediately.
tokenOnce: Copy the token now: it won't be shown again. If you lose it, revoke the client and create a new one.
jsonHelp: For other clients that accept an mcpServers block.
copiedWithoutToken: Copied with “<token>” in place of the token: replace it with the one you saved when creating the client.
activityHelp: Every client call is logged on this machine (the last 10,000 are kept).
approveAllOn: Approving everything until DBine is closed
approveAllOffTitle: Ask for approval again for each write from this client

approval.title: “{{client}}” wants to modify {{connection}} · {{database}}
approval.intro: {{client}} asked to run this code on {{engine}}. Nothing runs until you approve it.
approval.countdown: If you don't respond in {{time}}, it is rejected.
approval.approveAllWarning: “Approve all” runs everything {{client}} asks for without asking, until you close DBine or remove it in Settings › MCP. The risk is yours: review what the assistant can do before choosing it.

connection.label: MCP access
connection.help: What assistants connected through MCP can do with this connection.
connection.capProd: It has the “prod” tag: over MCP it never goes beyond read.
connection.capReadOnly: It is read-only: over MCP it never goes beyond read.
connection.serverOff: The MCP server is off: turn it on in Settings › MCP.

setup.title: How to connect it
setup.help: Pick your assistant and copy the matching snippet. Replace <token> with the client's token (shown only once, when you create it).
setup.claudeDesktop: Paste it into claude_desktop_config.json (Settings → Developer → Edit Config) and restart Claude Desktop. It needs Node: mcp-remote acts as a bridge.
setup.cursor: Paste it into ~/.cursor/mcp.json (or .cursor/mcp.json inside a project).
setup.vscode: Run it in a terminal (Copilot uses it in agent mode).
setup.chatgpt: ChatGPT can't connect: it calls MCP servers from OpenAI's servers and needs a public URL, and DBine's server listens only on this machine on purpose. To use an OpenAI model, use Codex.
